caption: 3 is not a quadratic residue mod 7
Listable in $n$: the residues mod 7 are 1, 2, 4
mathlib4.note: compute-engine's LegendreSymbol is Listable and threads over the list; Mathlib's jacobiSym takes scalars only.

caption: $-1$ is a residue mod $p$ exactly when $p\equiv1\pmod4$
Euler's criterion: $(a/p)\equiv a^{(p-1)/2}\pmod p$, here $3^3\equiv6\equiv-1$. See [[PowerMod]]
9 is not prime, so the call stays symbolic; see [[JacobiSymbol]]
wolfram.note: compute-engine's LegendreSymbol declines a non-prime modulus (per this example's name); Wolfram has no separate LegendreSymbol, so the emit uses JacobiSymbol (its closest counterpart), which is defined for any odd modulus and computes 1.
sage.note: Both decline: Sage raises ValueError: p must be a prime; ours leaves [LegendreSymbol,2,9].
sympy.note: Both decline: ours stays unevaluated, SymPy raises (ValueError).
mathlib4.note: 9 is not prime, so ours leaves the Legendre symbol unevaluated; the template reads Mathlib's jacobiSym, which accepts any natural modulus and gives (2/3)^2 = 1.
